Rachel — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and two asks so we can pick the right Dedicated configuration for the POC.

Recap (high level):
- ProdScale needs real-time text classification + short generation for support routing and summary.
- Target latency SLA: 95th percentile <= 150ms for single-turn gen (avg request size ~250 tokens).
- Expected steady-state: ~120 TPS peak, with 3x burst headroom. Token mix: ~70% short (<=128 tokens), 30% longer (up to 1k tokens) during nightly reprocessing.

Two asks:
1) Narrow the GPU family recommendation (A100 vs H100) given our mix and 95p latency target. Cost is very sensitive; we want a competitive reserved price but parity on latency.
2) Confirm concurrency model: should we expect 8-way concurrency per GPU or higher with batching + KV caching? Any guidance on how to size pool (number of GPUs) to hit 120 TPS steady-state with our token mix?

Also attaching the token profile CSV we exported from our analytics. Can you advise whether Hosted API could meet latency at our cost target or if Dedicated is clearly required?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up call.

— Samantha

Hi Samantha — really appreciate the detailed token profile. Quick high-level guidance and proposed next steps below.

Short answer: Dedicated is recommended for predictable 95p latency at your TPS with burst headroom, and for meeting cost targets once you commit to reserved capacity. Hosted could work for an initial short spike but will be risky for sustained 120 TPS with strict 95p latency.

Recommendation (initial POC):
- GPU family: H100 80GB preferred for latency headroom on mixed token shapes; consider A100 if budget is constrained and you accept slightly higher batch-induced latency on long requests.
- Concurrency model: plan for ~6-8 concurrent streams per GPU for mixed workloads; with continuous batching and prefix caching we typically observe ~1.8–2.2x throughput improvement vs naive single-request serving on H100.
- Pool sizing (ballpark): to hit 120 TPS steady-state and support 3x bursts, start with 8 H100s reserved (targeting ~15 TPS steady per GPU after batching/kv improvements). If choosing A100, start with 10–12.
- Token mix handling: enable KV prefix caching for short conversational requests; route long reprocessing jobs to a lower-cost pool (batch-only) or scheduled off-peak.

Operational asks / POC scope:
- Redwood provides: a reserved pool (VPC option available), baseline autoscale config, and monitoring dashboards.
- ProdScale to provide: representative traffic replay (we can accept redacted logs) and an SLO-based test plan for the POC.

Next steps I propose:
1) Technical deep-dive with our infra lead to validate the 8 H100 sizing (30–45 minutes) — suggested attendees: Rachel (me), Ben Carter (infra), Evelyn Hart (solutions), Samantha, Michael.
2) Share a draft POC statement of work + reserved quote (I attached a high-level pricing/tiers PDF).
3) ProdScale to confirm a week for traffic replay and security questionnaire recipients.

Attaching: redwood_dedicated_tiers.pdf (pricing tiers & H100/A100 tradeoffs), pooled_gpu-recommendation-20261204.xlsx (ballpark math).

If helpful I can also run a quick script to run your CSV through our throughput estimator and return a short table of expected TPS per GPU family. Want me to do that prior to the deep dive?

Best —
Rachel Kim

Ben / Evelyn — forwarding the ProdScale token profile and my recommended sizing. Two quick technical notes before the deep dive: please review and flag anything we should change in the sizing or assumptions.

Key assumptions I used in the spreadsheet:
- 250 avg request tokens for gen path, 95% of requests below 512 tokens except scheduled reprocessing windows.
- 95p latency target 150ms maps to service-level CPU+GPU queueing allowance of ~40–60ms and 90–110ms GPU inference time depending on model variant.
- Batch window aggressive at 8–12ms for high-throughput short tokens; longer requests batched separately.

Questions for you:
1) With our kernel selection on H100, are we comfortable claiming the 2.0x throughput gain in production for this token shape? If not, what guardrail should we use for quoting?
2) Does our autoscaler have a recommended warm pool size to hit 3x burst without cold starts? (ProdScale cares about burst headroom.)

If you can reply with quick notes I will consolidate into the POC SOW and send to Samantha.

— Rachel
